'''Wingate''' is a [[List of Brooklyn neighborhoods|neighborhood]] in the north central portion of the [[New York City]] [[Boroughs of New York City|borough]] of [[Brooklyn]]. The area is bordered by [[Prospect Lefferts Gardens]] to the west, [[Crown Heights, Brooklyn|Crown Heights]] to the north and east, and [[East Flatbush, Brooklyn|East Flatbush]] to the south. Wingate is bounded by [[Empire Boulevard]] to the north, Troy Avenue to the east, Winthrop Street to the south, and New York Avenue to the west.<ref name=Encyclopedia>{{cite enc-nyc|page=1267}}</ref> The area is part of [[Brooklyn Community Board 9|Brooklyn Community District 9]].<ref>[http://www.nyc.gov/html/cau/html/cb/cb_brooklyn.shtml Brooklyn Community Boards] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071221003420/http://www.nyc.gov/html/cau/html/cb/cb_brooklyn.shtml |date=2007-12-21 }}, [[New York City]]. Accessed December 31, 2007.</ref> It is sometimes considered part of Crown Heights, East Flatbush, and/or Prospect Lefferts Gardens.<ref name="Holland"/>

The neighborhood was originally named Pigtown because it was the location of several major [[pig farming|pig farm]]s that supplied Brooklyn.<ref name=Holland>{{cite web|last=Holland|first=Joy|title=Pigtown|url=http://brooklynology.brooklynpubliclibrary.org/post/2009/03/05/Pigtown.aspx|work=Brooklynology|publisher=Brooklyn Public Library|access-date=16 January 2013|archive-date=18 January 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150118174431/http://brooklynology.brooklynpubliclibrary.org/post/2009/03/05/Pigtown.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref> Pigtown was at the southern periphery of the [[City of Brooklyn]] where it bordered the [[Political subdivisions of New York State#Town|Town]] of [[Flatbush, Brooklyn|Flatbush]]. On modern maps it is bounded on the north by Empire Boulevard (formerly Malbone Street), on the south by Midwood Street, on the east by Albany Avenue and on the west by [[Nostrand Avenue]]. Future [[drag racer]] [[Frederick DiNome]] and his criminal brother [[Richard DiNome]] were born and raised in Pigtown,<ref name=Holland/> as was [[Rudy Giuliani]], who spent his first seven years there.

The neighborhood was renamed to Wingate in the 2000s by real estate developers, named for the park and the now-defunct [[George W. Wingate High School]], locally called "The Banjo School" because of its shape.<ref name=Encyclopedia/><ref>[https://www.nycgovparks.org/parks/wingate-park/history Wingate Park], [[New York City Department of Parks and Recreation]]. Accessed December 11, 2025. "The former hospital buildings were demolished to make way for the construction of George W. Wingate High School in 1954. This area was called Pigtown after its numerous small animal farms well into the 20th century. Eventually, the neighborhood adopted the name of Wingate after the school and adjoining park."</ref>
